notes: Upgraded from reproduced to verified (exact: true, we* + @mizopl, 2026-11-10, 7.2 s on one core under the default 900 s budget, zero floating-point arithmetic) via verify_challenge/cert_qubit_galois_m5_m6_rank4.py: slicing along qubits 1, 2 uses chi(H^4) = 4 (Fact 1) and chi(H^3) = 3 (Fact 2), excludes B-line terms (0 exact hits at ratio^(+-2) on the 2 G_3-orbits of |H>^3 rank-3 decompositions), enumerates all 4-covers of |H>^3 on D_3 (|G_3| = 48: 2,406 Kind-A orbits, 0 Kind-B, 6 Kind-C excluded by orthogonal Pauli support >= 4 > 2 at slice 11), and finds 30 slice-01 survivors and 0 5-qubit completions. Prior reproduced record (verify_challenge/cert_qubit_h_m5_lift.py, budget_s: 3600): chi(H^4) = 4 exactly (Lean tensor-square witness and the rank-3 exclusion over 36720 states). A rank-4 decomposition of |H>^5 sliced along one qubit has slice 0 a rank-4 decomposition of |H>^4 and slice 1 a Pauli image of it, term by term, times a fourth root of unity. |H>^4 has 30 rank-4 decompositions up to its unitary symmetries (group of order 384, 246 pivot orbits) and no Pauli assignment satisfies the slice-1 equation for any of them. Bravyi, Smith, and Smolin's rank-6 decomposition is the upper bound, so the cell is 5 <= chi <= 6; whether chi(H^5) is 5 or 6 is open, and a rank-5 witness would give exponent log2(5)/5 = 0.464. The certificate declares the 3600 s budget: the qubit H-type symmetry group is small and the enumeration ran 1649 s on four loaded cores.
